item.title: Today's Headlines - March 20, 2026
item.description:
World News

Israel and Iran conflict widens around Gulf energy sites

NPR reports Israel launched new strikes around Tehran while Iran continued attacks targeting Gulf energy infrastructure, including facilities tied to regional oil and gas exports. The escalation deepened concerns about broader regional spillover and global energy disruption.

U.S. Politics

Bipartisan talks intensify as Homeland Security shutdown drags on

NBC News reports Senate negotiators and White House border czar Tom Homan held new closed-door talks as the Department of Homeland Security shutdown stretched past a month. Senate leaders signaled they could cancel recess if lawmakers fail to reach a funding deal quickly.

item.title: Today's Headlines - March 19, 2026
item.description:
World News

Trump criticizes NATO allies for refusing to join Iran operation

Reuters reports President Trump said most NATO allies declined to participate militarily in the Iran conflict, calling the decision a major strategic mistake. The split has intensified tensions over burden-sharing and maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz.

Russia says it repelled one of the biggest drone attacks on Moscow in a year

Reuters reports Russian officials said air defenses intercepted about 250 drones approaching Moscow over two days. The escalation highlights how long-range drone warfare is widening risks for major population and transport hubs.

item.title: Today's Headlines - March 18, 2026
item.description:
World News

Putin agrees to temporary halt on energy facility strikes in Ukraine

Russia said Vladimir Putin agreed to pause attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure for 30 days after a call with President Trump. Reuters reports that Moscow did not accept a full ceasefire, while Kyiv said it would back the limited energy-strike pause.

US Politics

Lawmakers split over public scrutiny of the Iran war

NBC News reports Democrats are pressing for public hearings on strategy, costs, and legal authority for U.S. operations tied to Iran. Republican leaders have resisted, arguing that open hearings could compromise operations and saying classified briefings are sufficient for now.

item.title: Today's Headlines - March 17, 2026
item.description:
World News

Israel Says It Killed Iran’s Security Chief Ali Larijani as War Enters 18th Day

Israel’s Defense Minister announced that Israeli airstrikes killed Iran’s top security official Ali Larijani and the head of the Basij paramilitary overnight, marking another escalation in the regional war. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called on the US and Israel to end the conflict and said the bloc is consulting with Gulf and Arab partners on diplomatic proposals.

item.title: Today's Headlines - March 16, 2026
item.description:
World News

US-Iran War Enters Third Week as Trump Seeks Coalition to Reopen Strait of Hormuz

The US military campaign against Iran entered its third week with no clear end in sight. President Trump called on allied nations to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but Japan, Australia, and other key partners have so far declined to commit naval forces. Iran has effectively shut down the waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil supply.

item.title: Today's Headlines - March 15, 2026
item.description:
World News

Iranian Aerial Attack Strikes Central Israel

Iran launched a new wave of missile and drone attacks against Israel on Sunday, with the Israel Defense Forces reporting rescue and recovery operations underway at several incident sites in central Israel. Israeli police confirmed a destroyed vehicle at the site of a projectile impact in southern Tel Aviv. The strikes are part of Iran’s ongoing retaliation against the US-Israel military campaign, now entering its third week.

item.title: Today's Headlines - March 14, 2026
item.description:
World News

US-Israel War With Iran Enters Third Week

The US-Israel military campaign against Iran, now in its 15th day, escalated sharply after US forces struck military targets on Kharg Island, the critical hub handling roughly 90 percent of Iran’s crude exports. President Trump said the US deliberately spared oil infrastructure but warned it could be targeted if Iran continues blocking the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s military warned it could strike ports in the UAE in retaliation, and smoke was seen rising from a major energy installation in Fujairah.

item.title: Designing a Scalable, Pod-like Data Lake on AWS for On-Premises Data
item.description:
Designing a Scalable, Pod-like Data Lake on AWS for On-Premises Data

A Modular Approach to Data Modernization

Migrating data from diverse on-premises systems, especially proprietary environments like SAS and traditional databases, to the cloud can be complex. This document outlines a scalable, modern data lake architecture on Amazon Web Services (AWS) that simplifies this process through a “pod-like” modular design.

By leveraging serverless AWS native services like Amazon S3, AWS Glue, and AWS Lake Formation, this architecture ensures flexibility, security, and cost-efficiency. The modular “pod” concept allows for the agile addition of new data sources and processing workflows, translating abstract architecture principles into a tangible, high-performing data platform.
